senses.gloss: m. (an adaptation of ἰδιώτης) private man (opp. to priest, officer &c.), commoner; ignoble, ignorant.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Samuel 18:23">Targ. I Sam. XVIII, 23</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Megillah 12b">Meg. 12ᵇ</cite>, a. e. (prov.) <he>הה׳ קופץ בראש</he> the lowest man rushes ahead (is the first to give an opinion).—
<cite ref="Yevamot 59a:13">Yeb. 59ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>כהן ה׳</he> a common priest, opp. <he>כהן גדול</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Moed Katan 1:8">M. Kat. I, 8</cite> <he>הה׳</he> the untrained tailor, opp. <he>אומן</he> the professional.
Ib. 10ᵃ היכי דמי ה׳ when do you call one a hedyot?—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 104a:12">B. Mets. 104ᵃ</cite> <he>לשון ה׳</he> the popular terms, v. <cite ref="D01129"><he>דָּרַשׁ</he></cite>.
Gen. R. s. 96 משל ה׳ a popular adage; a. fr.—Pl. (Ch.) הֶדְיוֹטִין.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 30:8">Targ. Job XXX, 8</cite>; a. e.—(Hebrew) <he>הֶדְיוֹטוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 10:2">Snh. X, 2</cite> (<cite ref="Sanhedrin 90a:17">90ᵃ</cite>) three kings <he>וארבעה ה׳</he> and four private persons.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 21b:19">Snh. 21ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>לה׳</he> for the common people (Samaritans).
<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 13:1">Tosef. Sabb. XIII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 14:1">XIV</cite>), 1; Y. ib. XVI, 15ᶜ top <he>שטרי ה׳</he> private (not Hebrew) writings; Bab.
<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 1:2">Ruth R. to I, 19</cite> <he>פדה ה׳</he> a cow of common stock (not trained for work).
